en.title: Emphasis and inversion
en.summary: English can change the usual order for emphasis; inversion puts the verb before the subject.

paragraphs: English can change the usual order to give emphasis. Inversion puts the verb or auxiliary before the subject.

items: **Never have I seen** such a view.

paragraphs: Inversion happens after negative adverbs at the start of a sentence, such as never, rarely and hardly, and after here and there. It is common in writing. A cleft sentence with it is also used: It was Anna who called.

blocks.html:
PatternExample
negative adverb, then inversionNever have I been so happy.
here or there, then the verbThere goes the train.
cleft with itIt was Tom who called.
